title: Awaitable-rejection tests omit forward fail-closed gate assertion
description: python/tests/timing/test_time_sync.py:747-752, 777-784: neither new persist/clear awaitable test asserts the forward gate — after poisoning, _ensure_persistence_healthy_locked (provisioning.py:435-437) must make any subsequent install/clear raise RuntimeError 'provision verifier is poisoned after persistence failure'. Without that pin, a regression that poisons state but drops the health gate (something advancing later — the core qzxv property) is uncaught.
close_reason: Completed: the forward fail-closed gate pin is added to test_provision_persist_hook_rejects_scheduled_awaitable (test_time_sync.py:761-764) — post-poison, verifier.install(...) and verifier.clear(...) must both raise RuntimeError 'provision verifier is poisoned after persistence failure' (the _ensure_persistence_healthy_locked gate at provisioning.py:435-437, the qzxv core property). A regression that poisons state but drops the health gate now fails the test instead of passing vacuously. Edge-review hardening also landed: the sibling clear-hook test (test_provision_clear_hook_rejects_scheduled_awaitable) got the same forward-gate pin for both install and clear entry points. Full timing suite 73 passed (was 70); ruff clean. 3x review (kimi-k3): pass1 correctness PASS (gate tracing: install provisioning.py:515, clear :647, both route through _ensure_persistence_healthy_locked before any other failure path); pass2 security PASS (drop-gate regression surfaces as TypeError not RuntimeError, caught; accepts() independently re-checks __persistence_failed closing the stale-install path); pass3 edge PASS (clear-path gate duplication confirmed as cheap hardening, no conflict with sibling assertions).
